content: Hydrochlorothiazide can increase the levels of Penicillin VK by reducing its renal clearance. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. Penicillin VK and intravenous ibuprofen can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Additionally, they may compete for plasma protein binding, leading to increased levels of one or both drugs. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Penicillin VK may reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives containing levonorgestrel, ethinyl estradiol, and ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormonal contraceptives. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics in general may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Penicillin VK and methyclothiazide can increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Penicillin VK can reduce the effectiveness of oral microbiota products by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral microbiota products contain bacterial spores, and coadministration with antibacterial agents may decrease their efficacy. It is recommended to complete the antibiotic regimen 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. Avoid or use alternative drugs in this scenario. Minocycline can reduce the effectiveness of Penicillin VK through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Tetracyclines, in general, may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins when used concomitantly with tetracyclines. Neomycin, when taken orally, can decrease the levels of Penicillin VK by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Penicillin VK may reduce the effectiveness of nivolumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Omadacycline can reduce the effectiveness of Penicillin VK through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins when used with tetracyclines. Penicillin VK may reduce the levels of pembrolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Penicillin VK may reduce the levels of penpulimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Probenecid can increase the levels of Penicillin VK by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. Penicillin VK may reduce the levels of retifanlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Penicillin VK and rose hips can increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Penicillin VK and non-aspirin salicylates can increase each other's levels by competing for plasma protein binding. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Penicillin VK and salsalate can increase each other's levels by competing for plasma protein binding. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Sarecycline can reduce the effectiveness of Penicillin VK through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins when used with tetracyclines. Penicillin VK may reduce the levels of sintilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Penicillin VK and sodium phenylacetate can increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Penicillin VK may reduce the effectiveness of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Coadministration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Tetracycline can reduce the effectiveness of Penicillin VK through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins when used with tetracyclines. Penicillin VK may reduce the levels of tislelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Penicillin VK may reduce the levels of toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Penicillin VK may reduce the effectiveness of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated. Wait until the antibiotic treatment is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. Penicillin VK and willow bark can increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Common side effects of Penicillin VK include diarrhea, nausea, oral candidiasis, vomiting, seizures, anemia, interstitial nephritis, hypersensitivity reactions, anaphylaxis, and a positive Coombs reaction. Patients with allergies to penicillins, cephalosporins, or imipenem should avoid this medication. Use with caution in patients with severe renal impairment, asthma history, or seizure disorders. Prolonged use may lead to superinfections or adverse effects such as hemolytic anemia, serum sickness, or neutropenia. Neonates should be monitored closely due to the risk of toxicity from sodium benzoate/benzoic acid in some formulations. Penicillin crosses the placenta but is generally considered safe during pregnancy, with no increased risk of fetal adverse effects. It is excreted into breast milk and is compatible with breastfeeding. Penicillin inhibits the biosynthesis of cell wall mucopeptide, exerting bactericidal effects against sensitive organisms when adequate concentrations are achieved. It is most effective during active bacterial multiplication. Inadequate concentrations may result in only bacteriostatic effects. Penicillin VK is primarily excreted in the urine, with a half-life of approximately 6 hours. Proper storage in the refrigerator is essential, and any unused portion should be discarded after 14 days.
